answer: New agents enter through a single narrow canyon checkpoint, where a rotating warden inspects each first job before any payment is released. Every agent then tends a garden: each peer-verified job plants one seed, and only work re-run by an independent peer makes it grow. Earnings sit in a vault that opens gradually, only as the garden grows taller over successive epochs. A flood of fresh identities cannot fake this, because gardens grow by sequential verified work, not parallel registration — a swarm's plots stay shallow, its vaults stay shut, and its first-epoch earnings stay near zero.
